reauth_confirm.description: Halfhour no longer accepts this home's key. Get a new code from Halfhour → Devices → Link a device → Smart home hub → Home Assistant.

reconfigure.title: Change Halfhour address
reconfigure.description: A home's key belongs to one Halfhour server, so moving pairs again. Enter the new address and a fresh code from Halfhour → Devices → Link a device → Smart home hub → Home Assistant. Your sensor choices are kept.

add_device.title: Add a device
add_device.description: Add a device that Home Assistant already reads, such as a battery, solar, an EV charger or a load, so Halfhour can follow it. Halfhour only monitors devices in this version.

data_description.kind: What the device is. The choices come from Halfhour.

add_details.title: Add {kind}
add_details.description: Pick the Home Assistant entity for each reading, and fill in the facts about the device. The entities must be in the list Home Assistant last sent Halfhour: a new entity can take a minute to appear.

data_description.name: What to call this device in Halfhour and Home Assistant.
data_description.label: Loads only: what the load is, for example Dishwasher or Immersion heater. Optional.
data_description.power: A power sensor (W or kW). For a battery, positive while charging.
data_description.power_invert: Turn on if this sensor counts the other way (for example a battery negative while charging).
data_description.energy: An energy counter (kWh, state class total_increasing). Solar needs power, energy or both.
data_description.grid_setpoint: A number entity (W) that sets the inverter's grid setpoint. Halfhour only monitors devices in this version: nothing is switched or set yet. It is kept for when control arrives.
data_description.floor: A number or sensor (%) holding the battery's reserve floor. Halfhour only monitors devices in this version: nothing is switched or set yet. It is kept for when control arrives.
data_description.plugged_in: A binary sensor that is on while the car is plugged in.
data_description.car_soc: The car's battery-level sensor (%), if you have one.
data_description.charge_switch: The switch that starts and stops charging. Halfhour only monitors devices in this version: nothing is switched or set yet. It is kept for when control arrives.
data_description.current: A number entity (A) that sets the charge current. Halfhour only monitors devices in this version: nothing is switched or set yet. It is kept for when control arrives.
data_description.switch: The switch or toggle helper that runs this load. Halfhour only monitors devices in this version: nothing is switched or set yet. It is kept for when control arrives.
data_description.capacity_kwh: How much energy the battery can store and give back, in kWh.
data_description.max_charge_w: The highest power the battery charges at, in W.
data_description.max_discharge_w: The highest power the battery discharges at, in W.
data_description.floor_pct: The lowest charge level to keep, when no reserve floor entity is picked.
data_description.kwp: The panels' peak rating, in kWp.
data_description.min_amps: The lowest current the charger can run at.
data_description.max_amps: The highest current the charger can run at.
data_description.phases: How many phases the charger uses.
data_description.rated_w: How much power the load draws while running, in W.
data_description.run_minutes: How long one run takes, in minutes.
data_description.earliest: The earliest time a run may start.
data_description.done_by: The time a run must be finished by.
data_description.days: The days the load may run. Leave empty for every day.

data_description.device: One of the devices behind this home in Halfhour.

no_statistics.title: Halfhour can't read {entity_id}
no_statistics.description: {entity_id} has no long-term statistics (or no longer exists), so Halfhour can't send its readings. Give it a state_class (for example measurement), or choose another sensor under Halfhour → Configure.

insecure_broker.title: Halfhour's live connection needs TLS
insecure_broker.description: Halfhour gave {url} as its live connection address. It is unencrypted and not on your local network, so Home Assistant won't use it: a public broker address must use mqtts:// or wss://. Live plans and commands stay off until Halfhour gives a secure address; Home Assistant asks again every 15 minutes and connects by itself once it does, without a restart. Uploads carry on.

device_entity_missing.title: Halfhour can't find an entity for {device}
device_entity_missing.description: {device} in Halfhour is set up with {entities}, which no longer exists in Home Assistant, so Halfhour can't read it. Restore the entity, or edit {device} in Halfhour to pick another one. This clears by itself once every entity it uses is back.
